results.cause: The deployment runs image "busybox:1.36" with command ["/app/payment-gateway","--listen=:8443"]. Plain busybox does not contain /app/payment-gateway, so runc fails with "exec: \"/app/payment-gateway\": stat /app/payment-gateway: no such file or directory" (StartError, exit code 128). The rule finding says exit 127, but the observed code is 128 (StartError). The diagnosis is the same: command not found in the image. Most likely the image field points at a placeholder or base image instead of the real payment-gateway application image.
fix: Set spec.template.spec.containers[name=gateway].image to the actual payment-gateway application image that contains /app/payment-gateway, instead of busybox:1.36.

If the image is correct but the binary is at another path, change containers[gateway].command to the binary's real path. Check by running the intended image locally, e.g. `docker run --rm --entrypoint ls <image> /app`.

Apply the change (e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/payment-gateway gateway=<correct-image>` or edit the manifest), then confirm with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/payment-gateway`.

results.cause: Migration 0042_add_orders_index fails with 'ERROR: relation "orders_idx" already exists' and exits 1. The migrate script as defined in the pod spec also hardcodes 'exit 1' after echoing that error, so it can never succeed as written. Rerunning will not help. The script itself must change, and the migration must tolerate an index that already exists.
fix: Edit the migrate init container args in deployment/orders-api (spec.template.spec.initContainers[name=migrate].args). Remove the hardcoded 'exit 1' and make migration 0042 idempotent, for example 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS orders_idx ...'.
If the index was already created by an earlier partial run, mark migration 0042 as applied in your migration tracking table instead of re-running it.
Apply the change (kubectl apply / kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/orders-api) and confirm the migrate container exits 0 and api starts.

results.cause: The startup script checks DATABASE_URL and exits 1 when it is empty. The log says "FATAL: required environment variable DATABASE_URL is not set". The container only defines env vars DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD and LOG_LEVEL; DATABASE_URL is not among them. The startup script also echoes the DB password to the logs (redacted in this evidence), which leaks a credential.
fix: Add DATABASE_URL to spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].env of deployment/checkout-api. Because it likely contains credentials, source it from a Secret, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab create secret generic checkout-api-db --from-literal=DATABASE_URL='<url>'`, then add `- name: DATABASE_URL` with `valueFrom.secretKeyRef: {name: checkout-api-db, key: DATABASE_URL}`.
Apply the change and roll out: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/checkout-api && kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/checkout-api`.
Remove the line `echo "db config: user=$DB_USER password=$DB_PASSWORD"` from the container args so the password is not written to logs, and rotate that password since it has already been logged.

results.cause: The registry answered "docker.io/library/busybox:1.36.1-uclbic: not found" (rpc error code = NotFound). The tag "1.36.1-uclbic" looks like a typo of "1.36.1-uclibc" ("uclbic" vs "uclibc").
fix: Correct the image tag in the deployment, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/storefront web=busybox:1.36.1-uclibc` (or set spec.template.spec.containers[web].image in the manifest and re-apply).
Confirm the tag exists before rolling out: `docker manifest inspect busybox:1.36.1-uclibc` or `crane ls busybox`.
Watch the rollout: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/storefront` (the Progressing condition currently shows ProgressDeadlineExceeded and will reset with the new ReplicaSet).

results.cause: The image field contains two tags: "busybox:1.36:latest". A reference may contain only one ':tag' after the repository, so it fails with "couldn't parse image name \"busybox:1.36:latest\": invalid reference format" (InvalidImageName). This is a syntax error in the spec, not a registry or credentials problem. It is often caused by appending ':latest' to a value that already includes a tag (e.g. in a template or CI variable).
fix: Set the container image to a single tag, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/notify-worker worker=busybox:1.36` (or busybox:latest if that was intended).
Update the source manifest/Helm values/CI template so the tag is not appended twice (repository and tag combined only once).
Because the Deployment hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded, verify the new rollout with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/notify-worker`.

results.cause: The node pulls through the registry mirror at registry-mirror:1273. That mirror answered "500 Internal Server Error" to the manifest HEAD request for billing/ui:3.2.0 (ns=registry.pfa-lab.invalid), so it failed to fetch the image from upstream. The upstream hostname "registry.pfa-lab.invalid" uses the reserved .invalid TLD, which never resolves. The registry hostname in the image reference is most likely wrong, and the mirror cannot reach it. If the hostname is intended, the mirror itself is failing.
fix: Correct the registry host in the Deployment's container image field (spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image) to the real registry, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/billing-ui web=<real-registry>/billing/ui:3.2.0`.

If registry.pfa-lab.invalid is intended, make sure the mirror registry-mirror:1273 can resolve and reach it. Check the mirror's logs and upstream configuration, and fix or restart the mirror so it stops returning 500.
After fixing, confirm the rollout with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/billing-ui`. If it does not retry quickly, delete pod billing-ui-599f78df5c-qhksw to force a fresh pull.

results.cause: The container command runs `stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 300M --vm-hang 0`, which allocates 300M, but resources.limits.memory is 200Mi. The process dies within about 9 seconds (started 19:37:42, finished 19:37:51) with reason OOMKilled, exit code 137, right after the log line "stress: info: [1] dispatching hogs: 0 cpu, 0 io, 1 vm, 0 hdd". The workload's configured footprint is larger than the limit, so this is a sizing problem, not a leak.
fix: Raise resources.limits.memory (and requests.memory) on container cache in statefulset/session-cache to cover 300M plus overhead, e.g. 384Mi or the rule's suggested 448Mi: kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset session-cache --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"448Mi"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory","value":"448Mi"}]'
Alternatively, if 200Mi must stay, reduce the allocation in args, e.g. change --vm-bytes 300M to about 150M so it fits under the limit.
After the change, confirm the pod is recreated and stays up: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status statefulset/session-cache (if it does not roll, delete pod session-cache-0).

results.cause: The container command deliberately allocates more memory than the limit allows. It runs `exec stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 250M --vm-hang 0` and logs "loading 250MB of order history into memory", but resources.limits.memory is 128Mi. Each start hits the limit, so the container ends with reason OOMKilled and exit code 137. This is a fixed allocation, not a leak: it is about twice the limit.
fix: Raise resources.limits.memory on container worker above the 250M allocation plus overhead, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/report-worker -c worker --limits=memory=384Mi --requests=memory=300Mi`. Avoid 256Mi, which leaves almost no headroom over 250M.
Or reduce what the process loads so it fits the current limit, e.g. lower `--vm-bytes 250M` to about 100M, or have the real app load order history in smaller batches.
After the change, confirm the pod becomes Ready and check actual usage with `kubectl -n pfa-lab top pod`, then right-size the request and limit.

results.cause: The container is configured to allocate 200MB ("exec stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 200M --vm-hang 0", log line "log-shipper starting, buffering 200MB of logs in memory"), but resources.limits.memory is "64Mi". It hits the limit within a second and is terminated with reason OOMKilled, exit code 137. The rule finding's suggested 128Mi would still be too low for a 200MB allocation.
fix: Reduce the allocation to fit the limit: change the args to e.g. --vm-bytes 48M (or lower the in-memory log buffer) so it stays under 64Mi.

Or raise the limit above the 200MB working set: set log-shipper resources.limits.memory (and requests.memory) to at least 256Mi, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/search-api -c log-shipper --limits=memory=256Mi --requests=memory=256Mi.
Pin the image to a specific tag instead of the untagged "polinux/stress" to avoid a re-pull on every restart.

results.cause: Container trainer requests cpu "4k" (4000 whole cores), which is almost certainly a unit typo for "4000m" (4 cores). The only node cannot offer that much, so scheduling fails with "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu" (66 times), and the Deployment hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
fix: In deployment/ml-trainer, change spec.template.spec.containers[name=trainer].resources.requests.cpu from "4k" (4000) to "4000m", or lower if the app needs less (a busybox sleep needs very little, e.g. "100m").
Make sure the new request fits the node's allocatable CPU (kubectl describe node), or the pod will still not schedule.

Apply the change, for example: kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/ml-trainer -c trainer --requests=cpu=4000m. Then confirm the rollout with: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/ml-trainer

results.cause: The pod's volume "templates" references configmap "email-templates", which does not exist in namespace pfa-lab. The kubelet has retried 942 times: "MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume \"templates\" : configmap \"email-templates\" not found". The rollout has since hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
fix: Create the missing configmap in the pod's namespace, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab create configmap email-templates --from-file=<templates-dir>`. The kubelet retries the mount automatically, so the pod should start once it exists.
If the configmap exists under another name, change spec.template.spec.volumes[name=templates].configMap.name in deployment/email-sender to the correct name, then reapply.
If the templates are optional, set spec.template.spec.volumes[name=templates].configMap.optional: true so the pod can start without the configmap.

results.cause: The deployment sets nodeSelector {"hardware": "gpu-a100"}, and the scheduler reports "0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector". The single node does not carry the label hardware=gpu-a100, and preemption cannot help. The container (busybox:1.36 running "sleep 3600") requests no GPU resources, so the selector looks unnecessary for this workload.
fix: If the pod does not need a GPU node, remove spec.template.spec.nodeSelector.hardware from deployment/video-encoder: kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment video-encoder --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector"}]'
If the node is the intended target, label it: kubectl label node <node-name> hardware=gpu-a100
If a differently labeled node is intended, change the nodeSelector value to match a label shown by: kubectl get nodes --show-labels
If GPU nodes are truly required, add an A100 node labeled hardware=gpu-a100 to the cluster.

results.cause: The readiness probe is configured as "HTTP /ready port=http", but the app only serves files from /www and creates only /www/healthz (log: "catalog-api listening on :80, health at /healthz"). Requests to /ready get "HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404" (38767 times). The port is correct: http=80/TCP and httpd listens on -p 80.
fix: Change the readiness probe path in deployment/catalog-api from /ready to /healthz: spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].readinessProbe.httpGet.path: /healthz (keep port: http).
Apply it, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment catalog-api --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/healthz"}]'
Alternatively, if /ready must stay, make the app serve it by also creating /www/ready in the container command (e.g. echo ok > /www/ready).

results.cause: The container sleeps 45 seconds ("ledger-api replaying journal, this takes about 45 seconds") before starting httpd on port 80. The liveness probe starts after initialDelaySeconds=2 with periodSeconds=3 and failureThreshold=2, so it fails with "connect: connection refused" within a few seconds. The kubelet then kills the container (exit code 137, previous run lasted 19:38:23→19:38:59, ~36s, under 45s). The probe port and path are correct (http=80, /healthz is created); only the timing is wrong. The logs never reach "ledger-api listening on :80".
fix: Add a startupProbe to container api: httpGet path /healthz port http, periodSeconds: 5, failureThreshold: 18 (allows ~90s). Keep the existing livenessProbe; it only takes effect after startup succeeds.
Alternatively, raise livenessProbe.initialDelaySeconds to at least 60 and failureThreshold to 3 or more.
Apply with kubectl apply (or kubectl edit deployment/ledger-api -n pfa-lab) and confirm the logs show "ledger-api listening on :80" and the restart count stops increasing.

results.cause: The liveness probe is set to "HTTP /healthz port=8080", but the app runs "httpd -f -p 80" and logs "inventory-api listening on :80". The container declares only http=80/TCP. Nothing listens on 8080, so every probe gets "dial tcp 10.244.0.12:8080: connect: connection refused". After failure_threshold=2 the kubelet kills the container, giving exit code 137 even though the app never crashed.
fix: In the statefulset/inventory-api pod template, change spec.containers[api].livenessProbe.httpGet.port from 8080 to 80, or to the named port "http".

Apply it, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset inventory-api --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/httpGet/port","value":80}]'. Then delete pod inventory-api-0 if it does not roll automatically.
Optionally relax the probe timing (initialDelaySeconds 3, periodSeconds 3, timeoutSeconds 1, failureThreshold 2 is aggressive) to avoid flapping restarts later.
